The petitioners have been brought on record as legal representatives of the deceased respondent No.2 in the proceedings before the Trial Court.

4. Heard the submissions of learned counsel, Sri.T.M.Nadaf for the petitioners and learned counsel,
Sri.Rohit L Sheelvant for respondent No.1.
Perused the writ petition papers.

5. It is forthcoming that the Trial Court while considering I.A.Nos.34 to 36 held as follows:
"Point No.1 :- The order sheet reveals that, when the matter was posted for arguments on merits, at the instant of claimant IA.No.27 to 29 are filed to lead further evidence which came to be allowed by order dated 24.08.2023.
Further the order sheet reveals that, IA.No.30 and 32 filed by the claimant are also allowed and certain documents were marked as Ex.P.100 to NC: 2024:KHC-D:18098 Ex.P.110.
The PW.1 was fully cross examined by the respondents.

sentences.text: By the present applications the respondent No.2(e) to 2(f) intends to reopen the case for the purpose of further cross-examination of PW.1 and also intends to confront the alleged mortgage deed bearing No.2144/1943 which bears LTM of Smt. Gopamma and Thippamma.
In the entire cross-examination of PW.1 has not admitted the said alleged mortgage deed.
The suggestions put to PW.1 as to execution of alleged mortgage deed is consistently denied by the PW.1.
It is pertinent to note that, already PW.1 was fully cross examined and alleged mortgage deed bearing document No.2144/1943 is already got marked as Ex.R.9 on behalf of the respondents.
Such being the case, the question of again reopening the case does not arise at all.
It is also pertinent to note that, the respondent No.2(a) to 2(f) have produced only certified cop of mortgage deed and the certified copy of thump impression of the said mortgage deed.
They have not produced the original.
Already the mortgage deed bearing document No.2144/1943 is got marked as Ex.R.9 and PW.1 was fully cross
-examined with respect to the said document.
Therefore, no purpose will be served by reopening the case.
Hence, the respondent No.2(a) to 2(f) have not made out grounds to allow the applications."

(emphasis supplied) NC: 2024:KHC-D:18098 6. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that PW.1 having deposed that she does not know about Smt.Gopamma and only the certified copy of the document bearing No.2144/1943 having been produced, the applicant has now obtained the certified copy of the left hand thumb impression of the said Smt.Gopamma and Thippamma and are seeking to produce the same and seek for an opportunity to confront PW.1 with the certified copies now sought to be produced.

7. Learned counsel for respondent No.1 vehemently opposes the applications and submits that the said documents are now once again sought to be produced and the petitioners had an opportunity to produce the certified copies on earlier occasion and PW.1 having been cross-examined with regard to the same, the question of permitting the petitioners to produce once again the certified copies of the said documents does not arise.

8. It is forthcoming that along with the applications, respondent No.2(d) has produced a NC:
2024:KHC-D:18098 document list, wherein it has been set out the documents that are now sought to be produced along with the applications which discloses that apart from the certified copy of the document bearing No.2144/1943, the original intimation issued by the Sub-register and certified extract of the left hand thumb impression affixed on the document No.2144/1943 are also sought to be produced.

9. Having regard to the fact that the petitioners and the respondent No.1 herein are rival claimants to the compensation in the proceeding before the Trial Court and the allegations of fraud also having been made, in view of the fact that valuable rights of parties are sought to be adjudicated in the proceedings before the Trial Court, as also keeping in mind that the petitioners are now producing Hanumantha Reddy S/O Sidda Reddy vs Smt.
